title.en: Blood, blood vessels, blood groups and lymph

text.en: Every minute your blood visits every cell in your body and returns. It carries oxygen and food, takes away waste and fights germs.

Blood is a fluid connective tissue made of plasma (about 55 percent) and formed elements: RBCs, WBCs and platelets.
RBCs (erythrocytes) are biconcave, lack a nucleus in mammals, carry haemoglobin and transport oxygen; they live about 120 days and are made in bone marrow.
WBCs (leucocytes) are colourless nucleated cells that defend the body; granulocytes are neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils, and agranulocytes are lymphocytes and monocytes.
Platelets (thrombocytes) have no nucleus, number 2.5 to 4 lakh per cubic mm and help in clotting.
Functions of blood: transporting gases, food, hormones and wastes, protection, regulating pH and temperature and water balance.
Arteries are thick, elastic and carry blood away from the heart; veins are thin, have valves and carry blood to the heart; capillaries are one cell thick and join arterioles to venules.
Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood and pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood, the exceptions to the usual rule.
Blood groups A, B, AB and O depend on antigens on the RBC and antibodies in the plasma; Karl Landsteiner introduced the idea in 1900.
O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient; mismatched transfusion causes agglutination.
Rh factor was discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener in 1940; Rh positive people have the Rh antigen on their RBC.
Lymph is a colourless fluid with fewer proteins that drains tissue fluid, carries absorbed fats from the intestine and defends against infection through lymphocytes.

problem.en: A patient has blood group B. From whom can she safely receive blood?

text.en: Group B has antigen B and anti-a antibody.

why.en: Antibodies in the recipient attack mismatched antigens.

text.en: She must not receive antigen A, so group A and AB are unsafe.
She can receive from B and O.

prompt.en: List three differences between an artery and a vein.

requiredIdeas.en: Artery carries blood away from the heart and vein towards it

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all arteries carry oxygenated blood

points.en: Arteries away from the heart, veins towards it, capillaries exchange materials.
O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient.
Lymph drains tissue fluid and absorbs fats.
